children: US specialty insurance firm's Q3 revenue rose 4.7% but slightly missed analyst expectations
Adjusted EPS for Q3 increased 8.5%, beating analyst expectations
Company returned $173.7 mln to shareholders via buybacks and dividends
Ryan Specialty sees 2026 organic revenue growth rate in the mid-single digits
Company expects 2026 adjusted EBITDAC margin to decline modestly versus prior year
CLIENT RETENTION AND NEW BUSINESS - Co said organic revenue growth was driven by new client wins, strong renewal retention, expanded relationships, and continued flow into specialty and E&S markets
CASUALTY LINES GROWTH - Co said most casualty lines grew, offset by a moderate decline in property portfolio
EXPENSES AND RESTRUCTURING - Higher compensation and restructuring expenses due to the Empower Program partially offset by lower acquisition-related expenses
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 9 "strong buy" or "buy", 10 "hold" and 1 "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the multiline insurance & brokers peer group is "hold."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Ryan Specialty Holdings, Inc. is $48.00, about 12.6% above its October 28 closing price of $42.62
The stock recently traded at 18 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 17 three months ago
